quotes.text: A pilot proves usefulness. It does not prove scalability. Scalability only exists when the surrounding operating model can carry the solution under heavier load across more boundaries with less shared context and still produce trusted outcomes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the core difference between pilot success and enterprise scalability.

quotes.text: Replication is about copying outputs. Scaling is about reproducing operating conditions. Those are not the same thing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: AI will help you scale whatever you have already built. If you have trust, it scales trust. If you have drift, it scales drift.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: A successful pilot proves usefulness, not scalability; enterprise scale requires ownership, lifecycle and decision logic to scale with the solution.
Workspace sprawl, data lineage gaps, ownership ambiguity, Power Platform environment chaos and hidden connectors are symptoms of one root cause: capacity that did not scale with demand.
Standardize the few controls that protect trust, allow bounded local adaptation, measure system health instead of adoption and fund capability before rollout waves.
hook: Many Microsoft 365 and Power Platform solutions shine in a pilot and then fragment when they roll out across the enterprise. This episode is for architects, platform owners and transformation leaders who need their successes to survive scale. Learn the five failure modes behind the scaling paradox and a practical model for scaling principles instead of copying solutions.
